label: Digital Transformation Business Case
description: Build a rigorous, board-ready digital-transformation business case: value drivers, cost-to-serve, build-vs-buy, change-and-execution risk, TCO/ROI and benefits realisation, and the target operating model.

claudeKnowledge.description: Vendor pricing pages and analyst TCO benchmarks (Gartner, Forrester, IDC); cloud-provider pricing calculators (AWS/Azure/GCP); industry productivity and cost-to-serve benchmarks; case studies of comparable transformations; CSRD/ESRS and ISSB IFRS S1/S2 disclosure expectations where the programme touches sustainability or technology-spend disclosure.

guidedInputs.label: Organisation Type & Sector
guidedInputs.description: What kind of organisation and sector is this business case for? Drives benchmark selection and the relevant operating-model archetype.

guidedInputs.label: Transformation Scope
guidedInputs.description: Which dimensions of the transformation are in scope for this business case?

options.label: Target operating model & ways of working

guidedInputs.label: Investment Horizon & Decision Stage
guidedInputs.description: What decision is this business case supporting, and over what horizon?

options.label: Concept / seed funding to scope and prove value

guidedInputs.label: Financial & Sizing Parameters (if known)
guidedInputs.description: Any indicative numbers that should anchor the model: budget envelope, headcount, current cost-to-serve, baseline revenue, hurdle rate / WACC, expected useful life. Leave blank to work from sector benchmarks.
guidedInputs.placeholder: e.g. Indicative capex envelope EUR 18m over 3 years; ~2,400 FTE; current cost-to-serve ~EUR 34 per transaction; hurdle rate 11% (WACC + risk premium); 7-year useful life on the platform; opex run-rate uplift not yet quantified.

guidedInputs.label: Known Constraints, Risks & Stakeholder Concerns
guidedInputs.description: Describe the legacy estate, organisational constraints, prior failed attempts, regulatory exposure, vendor lock-in, change-saturation, or board scepticism that the business case must address head-on.
guidedInputs.placeholder: e.g. Two prior ERP attempts written off; heavy customisation on a 19-year-old core; CFO wants benefits booked, not 'enablement' soft benefits; data quality poor (no single customer view); DORA + NIS2 ICT-resilience obligations in scope; change-saturation after a recent reorg.

exampleInput: We are a mid-market Nordic commercial insurer (~2,400 FTE, EUR 1.1bn GWP) running a 19-year-old policy-administration core with heavy customisation. The board has asked for a business case to modernise: replace the core, build a single customer view, and stand up a GenAI-assisted claims and underwriting support layer. Two prior core-replacement attempts were written off. The CFO is openly sceptical of 'enablement' benefits and wants hard, bookable savings tied to cost-to-serve and loss-ratio improvement. We have an indicative capex envelope of EUR 18m over three years but no validated opex impact. Build-vs-buy is genuinely open — there are two strong SaaS policy-admin vendors and an in-house build option. DORA and NIS2 ICT-resilience obligations are in scope, and we are change-saturated after a 2025 reorganisation. Produce a board-ready business case with a quantified value model, TCO/ROI, a defensible build-vs-buy recommendation, the execution-risk picture, a benefits-realisation plan, and the target operating model.

exampleValues.financial_parameters: Indicative capex envelope EUR 18m over 3 years; ~2,400 FTE; EUR 1.1bn GWP; current cost-to-serve high vs peers; hurdle rate 11%; 7-year useful life on the new core; opex impact not yet validated.
exampleValues.known_constraints: Two prior core-replacement attempts written off. 19-year-old heavily customised core. CFO wants bookable savings, not soft 'enablement' benefits. No single customer view; data quality poor. DORA + NIS2 ICT-resilience obligations in scope. Change-saturated after a 2025 reorg. Build-vs-buy genuinely open: two SaaS vendors vs in-house build.
